Strait of Hormuz Status: October 14, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  227 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
14 October 2026 .
Brent $ 106.29 + 0.49 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Reuters reports Iran is shifting tactics to intensify attacks on shipping ahead of the US vote, per officials.

02 Anadolu Ajansı reports Iranian attacks targeted six ships near the Strait of Hormuz in a single day, the highest count since the war began, per Caspian Post.

03 Brent crude stood at $106.29, up 0.49%, as of 00:08 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded four transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains under acute pressure as Reuters reports that Iranian forces are shifting tactics to escalate attacks on commercial shipping in the period before the US vote, citing officials. A US official told Newsquawk that Washington is closely monitoring what it called unjustified acts of aggression against maritime shipping in the strait. The pace of incidents reported in this window is high: Caspian Post, citing Anadolu Ajansı, reports Iranian attacks targeted six vessels near the strait in a single day. Separately, Rudaw reports UKMTO logged three vessels struck by unknown projectiles, reported on October 12; Middle East Eye, Arab News, and Anadolu Ajansı report a UK maritime agency said a container ship and a tanker were hit by unknown projectiles; and Anadolu Ajansı reports the Iranian Navy said a tanker caught fire east of the strait, a separate development from the projectile strikes. The attacker has not been identified in UKMTO reporting. India's condemnation of strikes on commercial seafarers, with two Indian nationals reported missing, remains a live diplomatic thread. Against this backdrop, Brent crude stood at $106.29, up 0.49% over 24 hours, as of 00:08 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded four transits on October 4, compared with a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The feed indexed 45 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 00:22 UTC, 120 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
